F1.locus: About, the purpose (¶ after the heading block)
F1.quote: The purpose of this interdisciplinary workshop is to facilitate discussion around writing assistants, thereby enhancing our understanding of their usage in writing process and predicting the consequences.
F1.claim: the series' statement of its purpose: an interdisciplinary workshop to facilitate discussion around writing assistants, their use in the writing process and its consequences
F1.lineage: what it is: a workshop series on intelligent and interactive writing assistants

F2.quote: To this end, we strive to bring together researchers from the human-computer interaction (HCI) and natural language processing (NLP) communities by alternating our workshop venue between HCI and NLP every year.
F2.claim: the series brings together HCI and NLP researchers by alternating its venue between HCI and NLP every year
F2.lineage: the venue alternates between HCI and NLP

F3.quote: Enriching Writing Ecosystems at … The Fifth Workshop on Intelligent and Interactive Writing Assistants … co-located with … The 39th Annual ACM Symposium on User Interface Software and Technology (UIST 2026) … Detroit, MI … Monday, November 2, 2026
F3.claim: the series' site announces the Fifth Workshop, "Enriching Writing Ecosystems", co-located with UIST 2026 in Detroit, on Monday 2 November 2026

F4.quote: Now in its fifth iteration, our workshop seeks to facilitate discussions on designing and building cohesive writing ecosystems
F4.claim: the fifth workshop's theme: designing and building cohesive writing ecosystems

F5.quote: In this hands-on, systems-centric workshop, we challenge the UIST community to explore and develop ecosystems of writing assistants through the lens of interoperability.
F5.claim: the fifth workshop is hands-on and systems-centric, on ecosystems of writing assistants and their interoperability

F6.quote: Joining the workshop does not require a paper submission.
F6.claim: the fifth workshop requires no paper submission; participants register through UIST 2026

F7.quote: In addition to HCI and NLP research, we welcome participants from fields such as the Education Sciences, English and Rhetoric, and Linguistics.
F7.claim: the fifth workshop welcomes participants from education sciences, English and rhetoric and linguistics beside HCI and NLP
F7.lineage: the venue alternates between HCI and NLP

F8.quote: Examples of new forms of human-machine collaborative writing. … Wordcraft (Yuan et al., IUI 2022) … From Crafting Text to Crafting Thought (Liu & August, In2Writing 2025)
F8.claim: the site shows as examples of human-machine collaborative writing four works, among them Wordcraft (IUI 2022) and a paper of the 2025 workshop
F8.lineage: authorship under machine participation, in the papers

F9.quote: Keynote Panel featuring Tom McGee, Max Kreminski, and Ken Arnold
F9.claim: the fifth workshop's keynote panel: Tom McGee, Max Kreminski and Ken Arnold

F10.quote: You can contact the organizers by emailing in2writing.workshop@gmail.com.
F10.claim: the site names a contact address for the organizers; the organizers' names are not in its text

F38.locus: Gunser et al., The Pure Poet, title and design
F38.quote: The Pure Poet: How Good is the Subjective Credibility and Stylistic Quality of Literary Short Texts Written with an Artificial Intelligence Tool as Compared to Texts Written by Human Authors? … Participants read 9 AI-based continuations and either 9 human-written continuations (Study 1, N=120) or 9 original continuations (Study 2, N=302). Participants’ task was to decide whether a continuation was written with an AI-tool or not
F38.claim: a 2022 reader study: participants read AI-based continuations beside human-written (N=120) or original (N=302) continuations and decided whether each was written with an AI tool
F38.lineage: the reader study: judging whether a text was written with AI

F39.quote: Results showed that participants generally had low accuracy for differentiating between text types but were overconfident in their decisions.
F39.claim: the readers had low accuracy in telling the text types apart and were overconfident
F39.lineage: the reader study: judging whether a text was written with AI

F40.quote: AI-continuations were perceived as less well-written, inspiring, fascinating, interesting, and aesthetic than both human-written and original continuations.
F40.claim: the readers rated the AI continuations lower in style than human-written and original continuations
F40.lineage: the reader study: judging whether a text was written with AI

F41.quote: This new technology requires the author, asan act of writing, both to configure a systemthat then takes over the transformation into areal text, but also to maintain strategies of traditional writing.
F41.claim: a 2022 paper: data-to-text technology requires the author to configure a system that writes the text and to keep traditional writing strategies
F41.lineage: authorship under machine participation, in the papers

F42.quote: Centrally, we report how participants perform integrative leaps, by which they do cognitive work to integrate suggestions of varying semantic relevance into their developing stories.
F42.claim: a 2022 study of machine-in-the-loop story writing reports integrative leaps, the writers' work of integrating suggestions into their stories
F42.lineage: the 2022 papers: co-writing, revision, story, science writing

F43.quote: creative writers face additional challenges, including maintaining narrative consistency, developing plot structure, architecting reader experience, and refining their expressive intent, which are not well-addressed by current LLM-backed tools.
F43.claim: a 2022 paper: creative writers' needs for narrative consistency, plot, reader experience and expressive intent are not well addressed by LLM-backed tools
F43.lineage: the 2022 papers: co-writing, revision, story, science writing

F44.quote: The authors of this paper, including a professional novelist, have examined the use of natural language processing to address the problems of novelists … Although this is a preliminary study

F45.quote: The collected human-model interaction dataset and system code are available at https://github.com/vipulraheja/IteraTeR .
